key_insight: GITIII is a lightweight, interpretable graph transformer that learns correlations between a cell's internal state and its spatial niche to infer single-cell-level interactions and quantify how neighbouring cells influence gene expression.
problem_solved: Existing spatial-transcriptomics methods struggle to infer directional, cell-level interactions transparently and scalably; GITIII addresses interpretability, per-cell influence quantification, and efficiency for large spatial datasets.
method: Self-supervised graph transformer that models cells as graph nodes with attention-based aggregation of neighbouring signals.
Learns joint representations of intrinsic cell state and local niche correlations, producing per-cell, per-gene influence scores from attention weights.
Lightweight architecture designed for scalability and interpretability, enabling direct inspection of learnt interactions without heavy post-hoc fitting.
impact: GITIII gives ML practitioners an interpretable, efficient tool to discover and quantify cell–cell interactions from spatial transcriptomics, facilitating mechanistic insights and downstream biomarker or perturbation analyses.
visual_elements: Schematic of graph transformer: cells as nodes, edges for spatial proximity, attention weights shown as edge thickness

paper_title: Inferring spatial single-cell-level interactions through interpreting cell state and niche correlations learned by self-supervised graph transformer
paper_authors: Xiao Xiao, Le Zhang, Hongyu Zhao, Zuoheng Wang
